3.722: But until that time there shall be a race
3.723: Of godless men, even when that fated day
3.724: Shall reach its end. For offering to God
3.725: Ye should not make till all things come to pass,
3.726: Which God aloue shall purpose not in vain
3.727: To be all fulfilled; and strong force shall urge.
3.728: And there shall be again a holy race.
3.729: Of godly men who, keeping to the counsels
3.730: And mind of the Most High, shall honor much
3.731: The great God's temple with drink-offerings,
3.733: With sacrifices of fat bulls, choice rams,
3.734: Firstlings of sheep and the fat thighs of lambs,
3.736: On the great altar. And in righteousness,
3.737: Having obtained the law of the Most High,
3.738: Blest shall they dwell in cities and rich fields.
3.739: And prophets shall be set on high for them
3.740: By the Immortal, bringing great delight
3.741: Unto all mortals. For to them alone
3.742: The mighty God his gracious counsel gave
3.743: And faith and noblest thought within their hearts;
3.744: They have not by vain things been led astray,
3.745: Nor pay they honor to the works of men
3.746: Made of gold, brass, silver, and ivory,
3.747: Nor statues of dead gods of wood and stone
3.748: [Besmeared clay, figures of the painter's art],
3.749: And all that empty-minded mortals will;
3.750: But they lift up their pure arms unto heaven,
3.751: Rise from the couch at daybreak, always hands
3.752: With water cleanse, and honor only Him
3.753: Who is immortal and who ever rules,
3.754: And then their parents; and above all men
3.755: Do they respect the lawful marriage-bed;
3.756: And they have not base intercourse with boys,
3.757: As do Phoenicians, Latins, and Egyptians
3.758: And spacious Greece, and nations many more
3.759: Of Persians and Galatians and all Asia,
3.760: Transgressing the immortal God's pure law
3.761: Which they were under. Therefore on all men
3.762: Will the Immortal put bane, famine, pains,
3.763: Groans, war, and pestilence and mournful woes;
3.764: Because they would not honor piously
3.765: The immortal Sire of all men, but revered
3.766: And worshiped idols made with hands, which things
3.767: Mortals themselves will cast down and for shame
3.768: Conceal in clefts of rocks, when a young king,
3.769: The seventh of Egypt, shall rule his own land,
3.770: Reckoned from the dominion of the Greeks,
3.771: Which countless Macedonian men shall rule;
3.772: And there shall come from Asia a great king,
3.773: A fiery eagle, who with foot and horse
3.774: Shall cover all the land, cut up all things,
3.775: And fill all things with evils; he will cast
3.776: The Egyptian kingdom down; and taking off
3.777: All its possessions carry them away
3.778: Over the spacious surface of the sea.
3.779: And then shall they before the mighty God,
3.780: The King immortal, bend the fair white knee
3.781: On the much-nourishing earth; and all the works
3.782: Made with hands shall fall by a flame of fire.
3.783: And then will God bestow great joy on men;
3.784: For land and trees and countless flocks of sheep
3.785: Their genuine fruit to men shall offer-wine,
3.786: And the sweet honey, and white milk, and wheat,
3.787: Which is for mortals of all things the best.
3.788: But thou, O mortal full of various wiles,
3.789: Do not delay and loiter, but do thou,
3.790: Tossed to and fro, turn and propitiate God.
3.791: Offer to God your hecatombs of bulls
3.792: And firstling lambs and goats, as times revolve.
3.793: But him propitiate, the immortal God,
3.794: If haply he show mercy. For he is
3.795: The only God, and other there is none,
3.796: And honor justice and oppress no man,
3.797: For these things the Immortal doth enjoin
3.798: On miserable men. But do thon heed
3.799: The cause of the wrath of the mighty God,
3.800: When on all mortals there shall come the height
3.801: Of pestilence and conquered they shall meet.
3.802: A fearful judgment, and king shall seize king
3.803: And wrest his land away, and nations bring
3.804: Ruin on nations and lords plunder tribes,
3.805: And chiefs all flee into another land,
3.806: And the land change its men, and foreign rule
3.807: Ravage all Hellas and drain the rich land
3.808: Of its wealth, and to strife among themselves
3.809: Because of gold and silver they shall come—
3.810: The love of gain an evil shepherdess
3.811: Will be for cities—in a foreign land.
3.812: And they shall all be without burial,
3.813: And vultures and wild beasts of earth shall spoil
3.814: Their flesh; and when these things are brought to pass,
3.815: Vast earth shall waste the relics of the dead.
3.816: And all unsown shall it be and unplowed,
3.817: Proclaiming sad the filth of men defiled.
3.818: Many lengths of time in the revolving years,
3.819: And shields and javelins and all sorts of arms;
3.820: Nor shall the forest wood be cut for fire.
3.821: And then shall God send from the East a king,
3.822: Who shall make all earth cease from evil war,
3.823: Killing some, others binding with strong oaths.
3.824: And he will not by his own counsels do
3.825: All these things, but obey the good decrees
3.826: Of God the mighty. And with goodly wealth,
3.827: With gold and silver and purple ornament,
3.828: The temple of the mighty God again
3.829: Shall be weighed down; and the full-bearing earth
3.830: And the sea shall be filled full of good things.
3.831: And kings against each other shall begin
3.832: To hold ill will, in heart abetting evils.
3.833: Envy is not a good to wretched men.
3.834: But again kings of nations on this land
3.835: Shall rush in masses, bringing on themselves
3.836: Destruction; for they'll purpose to despoil
3.837: The great God's temple and the noblest men.
3.838: What time they reach the land, polluted kings
3.839: Shall set around the city each his throne
3.840: And have his people that obey not God.
3.841: And then shall God speak with a mighty voice
3.842: To all rude people of an empty mind,
3.843: And judgment from the mighty God shall come
3.844: Upon them, and they all shall be destroyed
3.845: By his immortal arm. And fiery swords
3.846: Shall fall from heaven on earth; and great bright lights
3.847: Shall come down flaming in the midst of men.
3.848: And in those days shall earth, all-mother, reel
3.849: By his immortal arm, and shoals of fish
3.850: In the deep sea, and all wild beasts of earth,
3.851: And countless tribes of winged fowl, and all
3.852: The souls of men and every sea shall tremble
3.853: Before the face of the Immortal One,
3.854: And there shall be dismay. Iligh mountain peaks
3.855: And monstrous hills shall he asunder break,
3.856: And to all shall dark Erebus appear.
3.857: And misty gorges in the lofty bills
3.858: Shall be full of the dead; and rocks shall stream
3.859: With blood and every torrent fill the plain.
3.860: And well-built walls of evil-minded men
3.861: Shall all fall to the earth, since they knew not
3.862: The law nor judgment of the mighty God,
3.863: But with a senseless soul all hurried on
3.864: Against the temple and raised up their spears.
3.865: And God shall judge all by war and by sword
3.866: And by fire and by overwhelming storm;
3.867: And brimstone there shall be from heaven, and stones
3.868: And great and grievous hail; and death shall come.
3.869: Upon the quadrupeds. And then shall they
3.870: Know God, the Immortal, who performs these things;
3.871: And wailing, and upon the boundless earth
3.872: Shall be at once a shout of perishing men;
3.873: And all the unholy shall be bathed in blood;
3.874: And earth herself shall also drink the blood
3.875: Of the perishing, and beasts be gorged with flesh.
3.876: And all these things the great eternal God
3.877: Himself bade me proclaim. And that shall not
3.879: Whatever only in my heart he put;
3.880: For truthful is God's spirit in the world.
3.881: But children of the mighty God shall all
3.882: Again around the temple live in peace,
3.883: Rejoicing in those things which he shall give
3.884: Who is Creator, righteous Judge and King.
3.885: For he himself, great, present far and wide,
3.886: Shall be a shelter, as on all sides round
3.887: A wall of flaming fire. And they shall be
3.888: In cities and in country without war.
3.889: For not the hand of evil war, but rather
3.890: The Immortal shall himself be their defender
3.891: And the hand of the Holy One. And then shall all
3.892: The islands and the cities tell how much
3.893: The immortal God loves those men; for all things
3.894: Help them in conflict and deliver them—
3.895: Heaven, and divinely fashioned sun, and moon.
3.896: [And in those days shall carth, all-mother, reel.]
3.897: Sweet word shall they send from their mouths in hymns:
3.898: "Come, falling on the earth let us all pray
3.899: The immortal King, and great eternal God.
3.900: To the temple let us in procession go,
3.901: Since he alone is Lord; and let us all
3.902: Meditate on the law of God most high,
3.903: Which is most righteous of all (laws) on earth.
3.904: And from the path of the Immortal we
3.905: Have wandered and with senseless soul we honor
3.906: Works made by hand and wooden images
3.907: Of dead men." These things souls of faithful meu
3.908: Shall cry out: "Come, having at the house of God
3.909: Fallen on our faces, let us with our hymns
3.910: Make joy to God the Father at our homes,
3.911: Supplied through all our land with arms of foes
3.912: Seven lengths of time in the revolving years;
3.913: Even shields and helmets and all sorts of arms,
3.914: And a great store of bows and arrows barbed;
3.915: For forest wood shall not be cut for fire."
3.916: But, wretched Hellas, stop thy arrogance.
3.917: And be wise; and entreat the Immortal One
3.918: Magnanimous, and be upon thy guard.
3.919: Send now against this city yet again
3.920: The people inconsiderate, who are come
3.921: Out of the holy land of the mighty One.
3.922: Do not move Camarina; for 'tis better
3.923: She be unmoved; a leopard from the lair,
3.924: Do thou not let an evil meet with thee.
3.925: But keep off, do not hold within thy breast
3.927: Ready for mighty contest. And serve God
3.928: The mighty, that thou mayest share those things;
3.929: And when that fated day shall reach its end
3.930: [And judgment of the immortal God shall come
3.931: To mortals], judgment great and power shall come
3.932: Upon men. For all-mother earth shall yield
3.933: To mortals best fruit boundless, wheat, wine, oil;
3.934: Also from heaven a delightful drink
3.935: Of honey sweet, and trees shall give their fruit,
3.936: And fatted sheep and cattle there shall be,
3.937: Young lambs and kids of goats; earth shall break forth
3.938: With sweet springs of white milk; and of good things
3.939: The cities shall be full and fat the fields;
3.940: Nor sword nor uproar shall be on the earth;
3.941: No more shall earth groan heavily and quake;
3.942: Nor shall war longer be on earth, nor drought,
3.943: Nor famine, nor the fruit-destroying hail;
3.944: But great peace shall be upon all the earth,
3.945: And king to king be friend until the end
3.946: Of the age, and o'er all earth common law
3.947: Will the Immortal in the starry heaven
3.948: Perfect for men, touching whatever things
3.949: Have been by miserable mortals done;
3.950: For he alone is God, there is no other;
3.951: And the stern rage of men he'll burn with fire.
3.952: But change entirely the thoughts in thy heart,
3.953: And flee unrighteous worship; serve the One
3.955: And deeds of lewdness; thine own offspring rear
3.956: And do not murder; for the Immortal One
3.957: Is angry with him who in these things sins.
3.958: And then a kingdom over all mankind
3.959: Shall he raise up for ages, who once gave
3.960: Holy law to the pious, unto whom
3.961: He pledged to open every land, the world.
3.962: And portals of the blessed, and all joys,
3.963: And mind immortal and eternal bliss.
3.964: And out of every land unto the house
3.965: Of the great God shall they bring frankincense
3.966: And gifts, and there shall be no other house
3.967: To be inquired of by men yet to be,
3.968: But what God gave for faithful men to honor;
3.969: For mortals temple of the mighty God
3.970: Shall call it. And all pathways of the plain
3.971: And rough hills and high mountains and wild waves
3.972: Of the deep shall be easy in those days
3.973: For crossing and for sailing; for all peace
3.974: On the land of the good shall come; and sword
3.975: Shall prophets of the mighty God remove;
3.976: For they are judges and the righteous kings
3.977: Of mortals. And there shall be righteous wealth
3.978: Among mankind; for of the mighty God
3.979: This is the judgment and also the power.
3.980: Be of good cheer, O maiden, and be glad;
3.981: For he who made the heaven and earth gave thee
3.982: Joy in thy age. And he will dwell in thee;
3.983: And thine shall be immortal light; and wolves
3.984: And lambs shall in the mountains feed on grass
3.985: Together, and with kids shall leopards graze;
3.986: And bears shall lodge among the pasturing calves;
3.987: And the carnivorous lion shall eat chaff
3.988: At the manger like the cow; and little children
3.989: In bonds shall lead them; for he will make beasts
3.990: Helpless on earth. With babes shall fall asleep
3.991: Serpents, along with asps, and do no harm;
3.992: For over them shall be the hand of God.
3.993: Now tell I thee a sign exceeding clear,
3.994: That thou may'st know when the end of all things
3.995: On earth shall be. When in the starry heaven
3.996: Swords shall by night point straight toward west and cast,
3.997: Straightway shall there be also from the heaven
3.998: A cloud of dust borne forth to all the earth,
3.999: And the sun's brightness in the midst of heaven
3.1000: Shall be eclipsed and the moon's beams appear
3.1001: And come again on earth; by drops of blood
3.1002: Distilling from the rocks a sign shall be;
3.1003: And in the cloud shall ye behold a war
3.1004: Of foot and horse, like the chase of wild beasts
3.1005: In the dense fog. This end of all things God
3.1006: Shall consummate, whose dwelling is in heaven.
3.1007: But all must sacrifice to the great King.
3.1008: These things I show thee, I who madly left
3.1009: The long walls of Assyrian Babylon
3.1010: For Hellas to proclaim to all the wrath
3.1013: And that I might to mortals prophesy
3.1014: Of mysteries divine. And men shall say
3.1015: In Hellas that I am of foreign land,
3.1016: Of Erythre born, shameless; others say
3.1017: That I'm a Sibyl, born of mother Circe
3.1018: And father Gnostos, raving mad and false;
3.1019: But at that time when all things come to pass
3.1020: Ye shall remember me, and no one more
3.1021: Shall call me mad, the great God's prophetess.
3.1022: For he showed me what happened formerly
3.1023: To my ancestors; what things were the first
3.1024: Those God made known to me; and in my mind
3.1025: Did God put all things to be afterwards,
3.1026: That I might prophesy of things to come,
3.1027: And things that were, and tell them unto men,
3.1028: For when the world was deluged with a flood
3.1029: Of waters, and one man of good repute
3.1030: Alone was left and in a wooden house
3.1031: Sailed o'er the waters with the beasts and birds,
3.1032: In order that the world might be refilled,
3.1033: I was his son's bride and was of his race
3.1034: To whom the first things happened, and the last
3.1035: Were all made known; and thus from mine own mouth
3.1036: Let all these truthful things remain declared.

4.1: People of boastful Asia and of Europe,
4.2: Hear how much, all too true, I am about,
4.3: Through a mouth many-toned, from my great hall
4.4: To prophesy; no oracle am I
4.5: Of lying Phœbus, whom vain men called god,
4.6: And further falsified by calling seer;
4.7: But of the mighty God, whom hands of men
4.8: Formed not like speechless idols carved of stone.
4.9: For he has not for his abode a stone
4.10: Most dumb and toothless to a temple drawn,
4.11: Of mortals a dishonor very sore;
4.12: For he may not be seen from earth nor measured
4.13: By mortal eyes, nor formed by mortal hand;
4.14: He, looking down at once on all, is seen
4.15: Himself by no one; his are murky night,
4.16: And day, and sun, and stars, and moon, and seas
4.17: With fish, and land, and rivers, and the mouth
4.18: Of springs perennial, creatures meant for life,
4.19: And rains at once producing fruit of field
4.20: And tree and vine and oil. This God a whip
4.21: Struck through my heart within to make me tell
4.22: Truly to men what things have now befallen
4.23: And how much shall befall them yet again
4.24: From the first generation to the eleventh;
4.25: For he himself by bringing them to pass
4.26: Will prove all things. But do thou in all things,
4.27: O people, to the Sibyl give an ear,
4.28: Who pours from hallowed mouth a truthful voice.
4.29: Blessed of men shall they be on the earth
4.30: As many as shall love the mighty God,
4.31: Offering him praise before they drink and eat;
4.32: Trusting in piety. When they behold
4.33: Temples and altars, figures of dumb stones,
4.34: [Stone images and statues made with hands]
4.35: Polluted with the blood of living things
4.37: They will reject them all; and they will look
4.38: To the great glory of one God and not
4.40: Of stolen gain, which things most horrid are;
4.41: Nor shameful longing for another's bed
4.42: Have they, nor vile and hateful lust of males.
4.44: Shall other men, that love a shameless life,
4.45: Not ever imitate; but, mocking them
4.46: With jest and joke like babes in senselessness,
4.47: They'll falsely charge to them as many deeds
4.48: Blameful and wicked as they do themselves.
4.49: For slow is the whole race of human kind
4.50: To believe. But when judgment of the world
4.51: And mortals comes, which God himself shall bring
4.52: Judging at once the impious and the pious,
4.53: Then indeed shall he send the ungodly back
4.54: To lower darkness [and then they shall know
4.55: How much impiety they wrought]; but the pious
4.56: Shall still remain upon the fruitful land,
4.57: God giving to them breath and life and grace.
4.58: But these things all in the tenth generation
4.59: Shall come to pass; and now what things shall be
4.60: From the first generation, those I'll tell.
4.61: First over all mortals shall Assyrians rule,
4.62: And for six generations hold the power
4.63: Of the world, from the time the God of heaven
4.64: Being wroth against the cities and all men
4.65: Sea with a bursting deluge covered earth.
4.66: Them shall the Medes o'erpower, but on the throne
4.67: For two generations only shall exult;
4.68: In which times these events shall come to pass:
4.69: Dark night shall come at the mid hour of day;
4.70: And from the heaven the stars and circling moon
4.71: Shall disappear; and earth in tumult shaken
4.72: By a great earthquake shall throw many cities
4.73: And works of men headlong; and from the deep
4.74: Then shall peer out the islands of the sea.
4.75: But when the great Euphrates shall with blood
4.76: Be surging, then shall there be also set
4.77: Between the Medes and Persians dreadful strife
4.78: In battle; and the Medes shall fall and fly
4.79: 'Neath Persian spears beyond the mighty water
4.80: Of Tigris. And the Persian power shall be
4.81: Greatest in all the world, and they shall have
4.82: One generation of most prosperous rule.
4.83: And there shall be as many evil deeds.
4.84: As men shall wish away—the din of war,
4.85: And murders, and disputes, and banishments,
4.86: And overthrow of towers and waste of cities,
4.87: When Hellas very glorious shall sail
4.88: Over broad Hellespont, and shall convey
4.89: To Phrygia sorrow and to Asia doom.
4.90: And unto Egypt, land of many furrows,
4.91: Shall sorry famine come, and barrenness
4.92: Shall during twenty circling years prevail,
4.93: What time the Nile, corn-nourisher, shall hide
4.94: His dark wave somewhere underneath the earth.
4.95: And there shall come from Asia a great king
4.96: Bearing a spear, with ships innumerable,
4.97: And he shall walk the wet paths of the deep,
4.98: And shall sail after he has cut the mount
4.99: Of lofty summit; him a fugitive
4.100: From battle fearful Asia shall receive.
4.101: And Sicily the wretched shall a stream
4.102: Of powerful fire set all aflame while Etna
4.103: Her flame disgorges; and in the deep chasm
4.104: Down shall the mighty city Croton fall.
4.105: And strife shall be in Hellas; they shall rage
4.106: Against each other, cast down many cities,
4.107: And fighting make an end of many men;
4.108: But equally balanced is the strife with both.
4.109: But, when the race of mortal men shall come
4.110: To the tenth generation, also then
4.111: Upon the Persians shall a servile yoke
4.112: And terror be. But when the Macedonians
4.113: Shall boast the scepter there shall be for Thebes
4.114: An evil conquest from behind, and Carians
4.115: Shall dwell in Tyre, and Tyrians be destroyed.
4.116: And Babylon, great to see but small to fight,
4.117: Shall stand with walls that were in vain hopes built.
4.119: But those from Susa and from Bactria
4.120: Shall all into the land of Hellas flee.
4.121: It shall take place among those yet to be,
4.123: O'erpouring to the sacred isle shall come.
4.124: And Cibyra shall fall and Cyzicus,
4.125: When, earth being shaken by earthquakes, cities fall.
4.126: And sand shall hide all Samos under banks.
4.127: And Delos visible no more, but things
4.128: Of Delos shall all be invisible.
4.129: And to Rhodes shall come evil last, but greatest.
4.130: The Macedonian power shall not abide;
4.131: But from the west a great Italian war
4.132: Shall flourish, under which the world shall bear
4.133: A servile yoke and the Italians serve.
4.134: And thou, O wretched Corinth, thou shalt look
4.135: Sometime upon thy conquest. And thy tower,
4.136: O Carthage, shall press lowly on the ground.
4.138: Shall earthquake lay low, casting headlong down,
4.139: But then, a city firmly set, again
4.140: Shalt stand. O Lycian Myra beautiful,
4.141: Thee never shall the agitated earth
4.142: Set fast; but falling headlong down on earth
4.143: Shalt thon, in manner like an alien, pray
4.144: To flee away into another land,
4.145: When sometime the dark water of the sea
4.146: With thunders and earthquakes shall stop the din
4.148: Also for thee, Armenia, there remains
4.149: A slavish fate; and there shall also come
4.150: To Solyma an evil blast of war
4.151: From Italy, and God's great temple spoil.
4.152: But when these, trusting folly, shall cast off.
4.154: Around the temple, then from Italy
4.155: A mighty king shall like a runaway slave
4.156: Flee over the Euphrates' stream unseen,
4.157: Unknown, who shall some time dare loathsome guilt
4.158: Of matricide, and many other things,
4.159: Having confidence in his most wicked hands.
4.160: And many for the throne shall stain with blood
4.161: Rome's soil while he flees over Parthian land.
4.162: And out of Syria shall come Rome's foremost man,
4.163: Who having burned the temple of Solyma,
4.164: And having slaughtered many of the Jews,
4.165: Shall bring destruction on their great broad land.
4.166: And then too shall an earthquake overthrow
4.167: Both Salamis and Paphos, when dark water
4.168: Shall dash o'er Cyprus washed by many a wave.
4.169: But when from deep cleft of Italian land
4.170: Fire shall come flashing forth in the broad heaven,
4.171: And many cities burn and men destroy,
4.172: And much black ashes shall fill the great sky,
4.173: And small drops like red earth shall fall from heaven,
4.174: Then know the anger of the God of heaven,
4.175: For that they without reason shall destroy
4.176: The nation of the pious. And then strife
4.177: Awakened of war shall come to the West,
4.178: Shall also come the fugitive of Rome,
4.179: Bearing a great spear, having marched across
4.181: O wretched Antioch, they shall call thee
4.182: No more a city when around their spears
4.183: Because of thine own follies thou shalt fall.
4.184: And then on Scyros shall a pestilence
4.186: Alas, alas! O wretched Cyprus, thee
4.187: Shall a broad wave of the sea cover, thee
4.188: Tossed on high by the whirling stormy winds.
4.189: And into Asia there shall come great wealth,
4.190: Which Rome herself once, plundering, put away
4.191: In her luxurious homes; and twice as much
4.192: And more shall she to Asia render back,
4.193: And then there shall be an excess of war.
4.194: And Carian cities by Meander's waters,
4.195: Girded with towers and very beautiful,
4.196: Shall by a bitter famine be destroyed,
4.197: When the Meander his dark water hides.
4.198: But when piety shall perish from mankind,
4.199: And faith and right be hidden in the world,
4.202: And reckless evil deeds, and of the pious
4.203: No one shall make account, but even them all
4.205: In childish folly, in their violence
4.206: Exulting and in blood holding their hands;
4.207: Then know thou that God is no longer mild,
4.208: But gnashing with fury and destroying all
4.209: The race of men by conflagration great.
4.210: Ah! miserable mortals, change these things,
4.211: Nor lead the mighty God to wrath extreme;
4.212: But giving up your swords and pointed knives,
4.214: Wash your whole body in perennial streams,
4.215: And lifting up your hands to heaven seek pardon
4.216: For former deeds and expiate with praise
4.217: Bitter impiety; and God will give
4.218: Repentance; he will not destroy; and wrath
4.219: Will he again restrain, if in your hearts
4.220: Ye all will practice honored piety.
4.221: But if, ill-disposed, ye obey me not,
4.222: But with a fondness for strange lack of sense
4.223: Receive all these things with an evil ear,
4.224: There shall be over all the world a fire
4.225: And greatest omen with sword and with trump
4.226: At sunrise; the whole world shall hear the roar
4.227: And mighty sound. And he shall burn all earth,
4.228: And destroy the whole race of men, and all
4.229: The cities and the rivers and the sea;
4.230: All things he'll burn, and it shall be black dust.
4.231: But when now all things shall have been reduced
4.232: To dust and ashes, and God shall have calmed
4.233: The fire unspeakable which he lit up,
4.234: The bones and ashes of men God himself
4.235: Again will fashion, and he will again
4.236: Raise mortals up, even as they were before.
4.237: And then shall be the judgment, at which God
4.238: Himself as judge shall judge the world again;
4.239: And all who sinned with impious hearts, even them
4.240: Shall he again hide under mounds of earth
4.242: But all who shall be pious shall again
4.243: Live on the earth [and (shall inherit there)
4.244: The great immortal God's unwasting bliss,]
4.245: God giving spirit life and joy to them
4.246: [The pious; and they all shall see themselves.
4.247: Beholding the sun's sweet and cheering light.
4.248: O happy on the earth shall be that man].

5.1: But come, now, hear of me the mournful time
5.2: Of sons of Latium. And first of all,
5.3: After the kings of Egypt were destroyed
5.4: And the like earth had downwards borne them all,
5.5: And after Pella's townsman, under whom
5.6: The whole East and the rich West were cast down,
5.7: Whom Babylon dishonored, and stretched out
5.8: For Philip a dead body (not of Zeus,
5.9: Of Ammon not true things were prophesied),
5.10: And after that one of the race and blood
5.11: Of king Assaracus, who came from Troy,
5.12: Even he who cleft the violence of fire,
5.13: And after many lords, and after men
5.14: To Ares dear, and after the young babes,
5.15: The children of the beast that feeds on sheep,
5.16: The very first lord shall be, who shall sum
5.17: Twice ten with the first letter of his name;
5.18: In wars exceeding powerful shall he be;
5.19: And he shall have the initial sign of ten;
5.20: And in like manner after him to reign
5.21: Is one who has the alphabet's first letter;
5.22: Before him Thrace and Sicily shall crouch,
5.23: Then Memphis, Memphis east headlong to earth
5.24: By reason of the cowardice of rulers
5.25: And of a woman unenslaved who falls
5.26: Upon the wave. And laws will be ordain
5.27: For peoples and put all things under him;
5.28: But after a long time shall he transmit
5.29: His power unto another, who shall have
5.30: Three hundred for his first initial sign,
5.31: And of a river the beloved name,
5.32: And the Persians he shall rule and Babylon;
5.33: And then shall he smite Medians with his spear.
5.34: Then shall one rule who has the initial sign
5.35: Of the number three. And then shall be a lord
5.36: Who shall for first initial have twice ten;
5.37: And he shall come to Ocean's utmost water
5.38: And by Ansonia cleave the refluent tide.
5.39: And one whose mark is fifty shall be lord,
5.40: A dreadful serpent breathing grievous war,
5.41: Who sometime stretching forth his hands shall make
5.42: An end of his own race and stir all things,
5.44: Putting to death and daring countless things;
5.45: And he shall cleave the mountain of two seas
5.46: And sprinkle it with gore; but out of sight
5.47: Shall also vanish the destructive man;
5.48: Then, making himself equal unto God,
5.49: Shall he return; but God will prove him naught.
5.50: And after him shall three kings be destroyed
5.51: By one another. Then a great destroyer
5.52: Of pious men shall come, whom seven times ten
5.53: Shall point out clearly. But from him a son,
5.54: Whom the first letter of three hundred proves,
5.55: Shall take the power. And after him shall be
5.56: A ruler, of the initial sign of four,
5.57: A life-destroyer. Then a reverend man
5.58: Of the number fifty. Next, succeeding him
5.59: Who has the first mark of the initial sign
5.60: Three hundred, shall a Celtic mountaineer,
5.61: Into the strife of battle pressing on,
5.62: Escape not fate unseemly, but shall be
5.63: Worn weary unto death; him foreign dust,
5.64: But dust that of Nemea's flower has name,
5.65: Shall hide a corpse. And after him shall rule
5.66: Another man, with silver helmet decked;
5.67: And unto him shall be the name of a sea;
5.68: And he shall be a man the best of all
5.69: And in all things discreet. And upon thee,
5.70: Thou best of all, above all, dark-haired one,
5.71: And upon thy shoots shall be all these days.
5.72: After him three shall rule; but the third one
5.73: Shall at a late time hold the royal power.
5.74: Worn out am I, thrice-miserable one,
5.75: Sister of Isis, to lay up in heart
5.76: An evil message, and an inspired song
5.77: Of oracles. First Mænades shall dart
5.79: And thou shalt be in evil hands that day
5.80: When the Nile some time shall fill the whole land
5.81: Of Egypt even to sixteen cubits deep;
5.82: It shall wash all the land, and water it
5.83: For mortals; and the pleasure of the land
5.84: Shall be still and the glory of her face.
5.85: Memphis, thou most shalt over Egypt wail;
5.86: For of old ruling mightily the land
5.87: Thou shalt become poor, so that out of heaven
5.88: The Thunderer shall himself with great voice cry:
5.89: "O mighty Memphis, who didst boast of old
5.90: O'er craven mortals greatly, thou shalt wail
5.91: Full of pain and all-hapless, so that thou
5.92: Thyself shalt the eternal God perceive
5.93: Immortal in the clouds. Where among men
5.94: Is now thy mighty pride? Because thou didst
5.96: And didst urge evil forward on good men,
5.97: Thou shalt for such things suffer penalty
5.98: In some like manner. No more openly
5.99: For thee shall there be right among the blessed;
5.100: Fallen from the stars, thou shalt not rise to heaven."
5.101: Now these things unto Egypt God bade me
5.102: Speak out for the last time, when men shall be
5.103: Utterly evil. But they labor hard,
5.104: Evil men evil things awaiting, wrath
5.105: Of the immortal Thunderer in heaven,
5.106: Worshiping stones and beasts instead of God,
5.107: And also fearing many things besides
5.108: Which have no speech, nor mind, nor power to hear;
5.109: Which things it is not right for me to mention,
5.110: Each one an idol, formed by mortal hands;
5.111: Of their own labors and presumptuous thoughts
5.112: Did men receive gods made of wood and stone
5.113: And brass, and gold and silver, foolish too,
5.114: Without life and dumb, molten in the fire
5.115: They made them, vainly trusting such things. . . .
5.116: Thmois and Xois are in sore distress,
5.117: And smitten is the hall of Heracles
5.118: And Zeus and Hermes (king). And as for thee,
5.120: (Of cities) war shall not leave, nor (plague) . . .
5.121: For thy pride thou shalt pay as many things
5.122: As thou before didst. Silent shalt thou be
5.123: A long age, and the day of thy return . . .
5.125: No more for thee shall flow luxurious drink . . .
5.127: For there shall come a Persian on thy dale,
5.128: And like hail shall he all the land destroy,
5.129: And artful men, with blood and corpses. . . .
5.130: By sacred altars one of barbarous mind,
5.131: Strong, full of blood and raging senselessly,
5.132: With countless numbers rushing to destruction,
5.133: And then shalt thou, in cities very rich,
5.134: Be very weary. Falling on the earth
5.135: All Asia shall wail on account of gifts
5.136: Crowning her head with which she was by thee
5.137: Delighted. But, as he himself obtained
5.138: The Persian land by lot, he shall make war
5.139: And killing every man destroy all life,
5.140: So that there shall remain for wretched mortals
5.141: A third part. But with nimble leap shall he
5.142: Himself speed from the West, and all the land
5.143: Besiege and waste. But when he shall possess
5.144: The height of power and odious reverence,
5.145: He shall come, wishing to destroy the city
5.146: Even of the blessed. And a certain king
5.147: Sent forth from God against him shall destroy
5.148: All mighty kings and bravest men. And thus
5.149: Shall judgment by the Immortal come to men,
5.150: Alas, alas for thee, unhappy heart!
5.151: Why dost thou move me to declare these things,
5.152: The painful rule of Egypt over many?
5.153: Go to the East, to races of the Persians
5.154: Who lack in understanding, and show them
5.155: That which is now and that which is to be.
5.156: The river of Euphrates shall bring on
5.157: A deluge, and it shall destroy the Persians,
5.159: And the Massagetæ that relish war
5.160: And trust in bows. All Asia fire-ablaze
5.161: Shall to the isles beam brightly. Pergamos,
5.162: Revered of old, shall perish from its base,
5.163: And Pitane among men shall appear
5.164: All-desolate. All Lesbos shall sink deep
5.165: Into the deep, and thus shall be destroyed.
5.166: Smyrna, whirled down her cliffs, shall wail aloud,
5.167: She that was once revered and given a name
5.169: Shall over their own country, then reduced
5.170: To ashes, wail, and o'er great Syria,
5.171: And o'er Phoenicia that has many tribes.
5.172: Alas, alas for thee, O Lycia;
5.173: How many evils does the sea contrive
5.174: Against thee, mounting up of its own will
5.175: Upon the painful land! And it shall dash
5.176: With evil earthquake and with bitter streams
5.177: On the rough Lycian land that once breathed perfume.
5.178: And there shall be for Phrygia fearful wrath
5.179: Because of sorrow for which Rhea came,
5.180: Mother of Zeus, and there continued long.
5.181: The sea shall overthrow the Centaur race
5.182: And barbarous nation, and beneath the earth
5.183: Shall tear away the Lapithæan land.
5.184: The river of deep eddies and deep flow,
5.186: Snatching men from the earth. Eridanus
5.187: (Pretending once to bear the forms of beasts).
5.188: Hellas thrice wretched shall the poets weep,
5.189: When one from Italy shall smite the neck
5.190: Of the isthmus, mighty king of mighty Rome,
5.191: A man made equal to God, whom, they say,
5.192: Zeus himself and the august Hera bore;
5.193: He, courting by his voice all-musical
5.194: Applause for his sweet songs, shall put to death
5.195: With his own wretched mother many men.
5.196: From Babylon shall flee the fearful lord
5.197: And shameless whom all mortals and best men
5.198: Abhor; for he slew many and laid hands
5.199: Upon the womb; against his wives he sinned
5.200: And of men stained with blood had he been formed.
5.201: And he shall come to monarchs of the Medes
5.202: And Persians, first whom he loved and to whom
5.203: He brought renown, while with those wicked men
5.204: He lurked against a nation not desired;
5.205: And on the temple made by God he seized
5.206: And citizens and people going in,
5.207: Of whom I justly sang the praise, he burned;
5.208: For when this man appeared the whole creation
5.209: Was shaken and kings perished—and yet power
5.210: Remained among them, and they quite destroyed
5.211: The mighty city and the righteous people.
5.212: But when the fourth year a great star shall shine,
5.213: Which alone shall the whole earth overpower
5.214: Because of honor, which was first assigned
5.215: To lord Poseidon; then a great star shall come
5.216: From heaven into the dreadful sea and burn
5.217: The vasty deep, and Babylon itself,
5.218: And the land of Italy, because of which
5.219: There perished many holy faithful men
5.220: Among the Hebrews and a people true.
5.221: Thou shalt be among evil mortals made
5.222: To suffer evils, but thou shalt remain
5.224: Hating thy soil; for thou didst have desire
5.225: For sorcery, adulteries were with thee
5.226: And lawless carnal intercourse with boys,
5.229: Thou city of the Latin land, unclean
5.230: In all things, Mænad having joy in snakes,
5.231: Over thy hanks a widow shalt thou sit
5.232: And the river Tiber shall lament for thee,
5.233: His consort thee, who hast a blood-stained heart
5.234: And impious soul. Didst thou not understand
5.235: What God can do, and what he doth devise?
5.236: But thou saidst, "I'm alone, and me no one
5.237: Shall sack," But now shall God, who ever is,
5.238: Thee and all thine destroy, and in that land
5.239: No longer shall thy ensign yet remain,
5.240: As of old, when the mighty God received
5.241: Thy honors. Stay, O lawless one, alone,
5.242: And mixed with burning fire inhabit thou
5.243: In Hades the Tartarean lawless land.
5.244: And now again, O Egypt, I bewail
5.245: Thy blind delusion; Memphis, first in toils,
5.246: Thou shalt be filled up with the dead; in thee
5.247: The pyramids shall speak a ruthless sound.
5.248: O Python, who wast justly called of old
5.249: The double city, be for ages silent,
5.250: So that thou mayest cease from wickedness.
5.251: Reckless in evils, treasury of toils,
5.253: Much-weeping, thou a widow shalt remain
5.254: Through all time. Thou didst full of years become
5.255: While thou alone wast ruling o'er the world;
5.256: But when the white dress Barca round herself
5.257: Shall put on over that which is defiled,
5.258: Would that I neither were nor had been born!
5.259: O Thebes, where is thy great strength? A fierce man
5.260: Shall slay the people; but thou, wretched one,
5.261: Grasping thy dusky dress shalt wail alone,
5.262: And thou shalt make atonement for all things.
5.263: Which thou aforetime with a shameless soul
5.264: Didst perpetrate. They also shall behold.
5.265: A mourning on account of lawless deeds.
5.266: And a mighty man of the Ethiopians
5.267: Shall overthrow Syene; by their might
5.269: Pentapolis, a man of mighty strength
5.270: Shall burn thee whole. All-tearful Libya,
5.271: Who shall explain thy follies? And Cyrene,
5.272: Of mortals who shall pitiably weep
5.273: For thee? Thou shalt not even to the time
5.274: Of thy destruction cease thy hateful wail.
5.275: Among the Britons and among the Gauls,
5.276: Rich in gold, Ocean shall be roaring loud
5.277: Filled with much blood; for evil things
5.278: Did they unto God's children, when a king
5.279: Of the Sidonians, a Phoenician, led
5.280: A mighty Gallic host from Syria;
5.281: And he shall slaughter thee, thyself, Ravenna,
5.282: And unto slaughter shall he lead the way.
5.284: Together fear; for when with these the course
5.285: Of Capricorn and Taurus in the Twins
5.286: Shall wind about the middle of the heaven,
5.287: Virgo then rising, and about his front.
5.288: Fastening a belt the sun shall lead all heaven,
5.289: There shall be moving downwards to the earth
5.290: A mighty conflagration high in air,
5.291: And a new nature in the warlike stars,
5.292: So that the whole land of the Ethiops
5.293: Shall perish in the midst of fire and groans.
5.294: And weep thou, Corinth, the destruction sad
5.295: Which is in thee; for when with pliant threads
5.296: The Fates, three sisters, spinning shall aloft
5.297: Lead him who flees by guile against the voice
5.298: Of the isthmus, until all shall look at him
5.299: Who once cut out the rock with ductile brass,
5.300: He also shall destroy and smite thy land,
5.301: As it bath been appointed. For to him
5.302: God gave strength to accomplish that which could
5.303: No earlier of all the kings together.
5.304: And first with sickle cleaving off the roots
5.305: From three heads he shall give food in excess
5.306: To others, so that kings unclean shall eat
5.307: The flesh of parents. For unto all men
5.308: Slaughter and terrors are laid up in store
5.309: Because of the great city and just people
5.310: Saved through all time, whom Providence held high.
5.311: O thou unstable one and ill-advised,
5.312: By evil fates surrounded, for mankind
5.313: Both a beginning and great end of toil,—
5.314: Of suffering creation and of part
5.316: Of evils, and for men a great curse, who
5.317: Of mortals wished for thee? Who has not been
5.318: Embittered from within? Cast down in thee
5.319: A king his honored life lost. Evilly
5.320: Hast thou disposed all things and washed away
5.321: All that is fair, and by thee have been changed
5.322: The world's fair folds. In strife with us perhaps
5.323: Thou hast brought forward these unstable things;
5.324: And how dost thou say, "I will thee persuade,"
5.325: And "If in any thing thou blame me, speak?"
5.326: There was once among men the sun's bright light
5.327: The prophets' common ray being spread abroad;
5.328: Speech dripping honey, fair drink for all men,
5.329: Appeared and grew, and day arose on all.
5.330: Because of this, thou narrow-minded one
5.331: Leader of greatest evils, both a sword
5.332: And grief shall come in that day. For mankind
5.333: Both a beginning and great end of toil,—
5.334: Of suffering creation and of part
5.335: Restored again,—hear, O thou curse of men,
5.337: But when the Persian land shall keep away
5.338: From war and plague and groaning, in that day
5.339: A race divine of blessed heavenly Jews
5.340: Shall offer prayer, who shall dwell round about
5.341: God's city in mid portions of the land,
5.342: And even as far as Joppa building round
5.343: A great wall they shall carry it aloft
5.344: Unto the gloomy clouds. No more shall trump
5.345: Sound battle-din nor by a foe's mad hands
5.346: Shall they be cut off; but they shall set up
5.347: Their trophies for an age of evil men.
5.348: And one shall come again from heaven, a man
5.349: Preeminent, whose hands on fruitful tree
5.350: By far the noblest of the Hebrews stretched,
5.351: Who at one time did make the sun stand still
5.352: When he spoke with fair word and holy lips.
5.353: No longer vex thy soul within thy breast
5.354: By reason of the sword, rich child of God,
5.355: Flower longed for by him only, goodly light
5.356: And noble branch, a scion much beloved,
5.358: Inspired by hymns, No more shall unclean foot
5.359: Of Greeks keep revel round about thy land,
5.360: Who held within their breast a lawless mind;
5.361: But thee shall glorious children honor much
5.362: [And be expert in songs and holy tongues],
5.363: With sacrifices of all kinds and prayers
5.364: Honored of God. All who endure the toils
5.365: Of small affliction and the just shall have
5.367: But the wicked, who to heaven sent lawless speech,
5.368: Shall cease their speaking one against another,
5.369: And hide themselves until the world be changed.
5.370: And there shall be a rain of gleaming fire
5.371: From the clouds; and no more shall mortals reap
5.372: The fair corn from the earth; all things unsown
5.373: And unplowed, until mortal men shall know
5.374: The Lord of all things, the immortal God
5.375: Always existing, and no more revere
5.376: Mortal things, neither dogs nor vultures' nests,
5.377: And what things Egypt taught to magnify
5.378: With dumb mouths and dull lips. But all these things
5.379: The holy land of the only pious men
5.380: Shall bring forth, from the honey-dripping rock
5.381: A stream and from a spring ambrosial milk
5.382: Shall flow for all the just; for in one God,
5.383: One Father, who alone is glorious,
5.384: Having great piety and faith they hoped.
5.385: But why does the wise mind grant me these things?
5.386: And now thee, wretched Asia, piteously
5.387: I mourn and the race of Ionians
5.388: And Carians and Lydians rich in gold.
5.389: Alas, alas for thee, O Sardis; and alas
5.390: For Trallis much beloved; alas, alas,
5.392: Thus shalt thou be by earthquakes overthrown
5.393: And ruined, and be also changed to dust.
5.396: By chasms and earthquakes shall come headlong down.
5.397: Sometime into the dreadful sea, as storms
5.399: Shall wail aloud, lament beside her banks,
5.400: And for her temple search which is no more.
5.401: And then ineensed shall God the imperishable,
5.402: Who dwells on high, burl thunderbolts from heaven
5.403: Down on the head of him that is impure.
5.404: And in the place of winter there shall be
5.405: In that day summer. And to mortal men
5.406: Shall then be great woe; for the Thunderer
5.407: Shall utterly destroy all shameless men
5.408: And with his thunders and with lightning-flames
5.409: And blazing thunderbolts men of ill-will,
5.410: And thus shall he destroy the impious ones,
5.411: So that there shall remain upon the earth
5.412: Dead bodies more in number than the sand.
5.413: For Smyrna also, weeping her Lycurgus,
5.414: Shall come unto the gates of Ephesus
5.415: And she herself shall perish even more.
5.416: And foolish Cyme with her inspired streams
5.417: Cast down by hands of godless men unjust
5.418: And lawless, shall to heaven not so much
5.419: As a word utter; but she shall remain
5.420: Dead in Cymæan streams. And then shall they
5.422: Cyme's rough populace and shameless tribe,
5.423: Having a sign, shall know for what they toiled.
5.424: And then, when they shall have bewailed their land
5.428: Alas for thee, cease from thy revelry.
5.430: With riches mixed, what thou hast longed to have
5.431: Thou shalt have, even a land of many tears,
5.432: Since thou wast angry towards a land beside
5.434: Beside the waters of Meander, thee
5.435: Shall by the nightly surges under shore
5.436: God's wrath and foresight utterly destroy.
5.437: Take me not, willing, to the neighboring land
5.438: Of Phœbus; sometime shall a thunderbolt
5.440: Because she seized on Phœbus' crafty song
5.441: And the wise care and prudent plan of men.
5.442: Father of all, be gracious to the land
5.443: Of Judah, well fed, fruit-abounding, great,
5.444: In order that thy judgments we may see.
5.445: For thou, O God, in kindness didst regard
5.446: This land first that it might appear to be
5.447: Thy gracious gift unto all mortal men
5.448: And to hold fast what God put in their charge.
5.449: The works thrice wretched of the Thracians
5.450: I yearn to see, and wall between two seas
5.451: Trailed in the dust along beneath the mist,
5.452: Even like a river for the swimming fish.
5.453: O wretched Hellespont, sometime a child
5.454: Of the Assyrians shall throw a yoke
5.455: Across thee; battle of the Thracians comes
5.456: And shall despoil thy strength. And there shall rule
5.458: A king of Egypt, and a barbarous clime
5.459: Shall waste the strength of captains. Lydians
5.461: With the Pisidians, all equipped for war
5.462: Shall in a mass bring evil strife to pass.
5.463: Thrice wretched Italy, thou shalt remain
5.465: By deadly sting to perish utterly.
5.466: And sometime high in the broad heaven above
5.467: Like thunder-roaring shall God's voice be heard.
5.468: And the unwasting flames of the sun himself
5.469: Shall be no more, nor shall the brilliant light
5.470: Of the moon again be in the latest time,
5.471: When God shall be the ruler. And dark gloom
5.472: Shall be o'er all the earth, and blinded men
5.473: And evil beasts and woe; that day shall be
5.474: A long time, so that men shall see that God
5.475: Himself is Lord, the overseer of all
5.476: In front of heaven. And then will he himself
5.477: Not pity hostile men, who sacrifice
5.478: Their herds of lambs and sheep and calves and goats
5.479: And bellowing golden-horned bulls, offering them
5.480: To lifeless Hermæ and to gods of stone.
5.481: But let the law of wisdom be your guide
5.482: And the glory of the righteous; lest sometime
5.484: Each race of men and shameless tribe of life,
5.485: It doth behoove them faithfully to love.
5.486: The Father, the wise God who ever is.
5.487: In the last time, at the turning of the moon,
5.488: There shall be raging through the world a war
5.489: And carried on with cunning and in guile.
5.490: And from the limits of the earth shall come
5.491: Fleeing, and pondering sharp things in his mind,
5.492: A matricidal man who every land
5.493: Shall overpower and over all things rule,
5.494: And see all things more wisely than all men;
5.495: And that for whose sake he himself was slain
5.496: Shall he seize forthwith. And he shall destroy
5.497: Many men and great tyrants and shall burn
5.498: All of them, as none other ever did,

12.264: Of the great pious king; and at the end

12.267: By his own lot and leave the royal power

12.271: Dominion. This man with superior powers
12.272: Of mind shall grasp all things; and he shall rival
12.274: And be the best in mighty arms and have

12.278: A fearful sign: there shall be a great mist
12.279: Then in the plain of Rome, so that a man
12.280: May not discern his neighbor. And then wars

12.283: And weakly, shall come in the marriage-bod
12.286: And then, in helpless loneliness concealed,
12.287: The mighty baneful man held under wrath

12.289: Man-slaying Ares bound by treacherous fate.
12.290: Know then the fatal lot of Rome is near
12.291: Because of zeal for power; and by the hands
12.292: Of Ares many in Palladian halls
12.293: Shall perish. And then Rome shall be bereft
12.294: And shall repay all things, which she alone

12.296: My heart laments, my heart within me mourns;
12.297: For from the time when thy first king, proud Rome,
12.298: Gave good law to thee and to men on earth,
12.299: And the Word of the great immortal God
12.300: Came to the earth, until the nineteenth reign
12.301: Shall have been finished Cronos shall complete
12.302: Two hundred years, twice twenty and twice two,
12.303: With six months added; then the twentieth king,
12.304: When smitten with sharp brass he with the sword
12.305: Shall in thy houses pour out blood, shall make
12.306: Thy race a widow, having in his name
12.307: The letter which the number eighty shows,
12.308: And burdened with old age; but he shall make
12.309: A widow of thee in a little time,
12.311: And murders, homicides, and deadly feuds
12.312: And miseries of conquests there shall be,
12.313: And in confusion many a horse and man
12.314: Shall, cleft by force of hands, fall in the plain.

12.316: The sign of his name in the number ten;
12.317: And many sorrows shall he bring to pass,
12.318: And groans, and he shall plunder many men;
12.319: But he himself shall be short-lived and fall
12.320: By mighty Ares, struck by gleaming iron.

12.330: A man skilled in fraud, full of various wiles,

12.332: The number of two hundred. And again
12.333: Another sign: he shall contrive a war
12.334: For royal power against Assyrian men,

12.337: But there is much contrivance in his heart,
12.338: Impulse of baleful Ares; serpent dire,
12.339: And violent in war, who shall destroy
12.340: All high-born men upon the earth, and slay
12.341: The noble for their wealth, and, robber like,
12.342: Stripping all earth while men are perishing,
12.343: He shall go to the East; and all deceit
12.346: Then shall a youthful Cæsar with him reign

12.348: Of Macedon, by the first letter known;

12.350: The hard deception of the coming king
12.351: In the bosom of the army; but the one

12.361: For you first once the yawning oarth received.
12.364: Shall wail . . . while men are perishing
